svg.title: Shift queue prioritisation and state
svg.desc: The working order for a shift queue, which is not strictly by severity. First, anything escalated to you from another tier. Second, High and Critical unassigned, newest first. Third, any severity on a host or account that already has an open incident, which is the line people get wrong. Fourth, High and Critical assigned to you, oldest first. Fifth, Medium unassigned. Sixth, Low and review feeds, batched once a shift. A worked example shows a Medium alert on a host that already has a High open being promoted above other High alerts. Three warning states are listed: an unassigned High older than one hour means the queue is not being worked, many incidents on one owner means redistribute, and Active with no update in eight hours is the worst state an incident can be in because it looks worked and is not.
svg.text: Working the queue
Not strictly by severity. Severity says how bad a thing is. It does not say what it enables next.
Order
Escalated to you from another tier
Somebody is waiting on you specifically
High and Critical, unassigned, newest first
Newest, because the attack is still in progress
Any severity, on a host or account already open
The line people get wrong. A Medium on a machine with a
High open is probably the next stage of the same intrusion
High and Critical, assigned to you, oldest first
Oldest, because the SLA clock is running
Medium, unassigned
Low and review feeds, batched once a shift
Why line 3 matters
High
INC-0412 WS11-01 Office spawned shell
Active, owned
Medium
INC-0417 WS11-01 Defender exclusion added
Same host. Promote above other Highs.
This is the step immediately before credential theft.
In IR-2026-014 this exact alert waited 71 seconds and the attacker used the exclusion.
Queue warning states
Unassigned High older than 1 hour
The queue is not being worked. Claim it or escalate.
Many incidents on one owner
Somebody is drowning. Redistribute before they miss one.
Active with no update in 8 hours
The worst state an incident can be in. It looks like it is being
worked and it is not. Comment, or put it back to New.
Sentinel handles most of line 3 automatically when
entity mapping is configured on every rule, because
alerts on the same host group into one incident.
Run the queue health query at the start of every shift. Three things to look for are listed on the right.
